title: Time Series in Emergency Medicine
text:
About the workshop
Emergency departments generate data every hour of every day. This workshop shows you how to explore, decompose, model and forecast that data using R.

title: Time Series in Emergency Medicine
text:
Objectives
At the end of the workshop, participants are able:

To understand concepts of time-series analysis and forecasting
To understand features and sources of time series data
To perform analysis of time series data using R
To appraise time-series and forecasting manuscripts
To understand concepts for GAM and joint-point regression

title: Time Series in Emergency Medicine
text:
Before you come
Please install the software on the Prerequisites page before Day 1. Slides, data and exercises are on the Resources page.

title: Prerequisites
text:
Please install these before Day 1. Each takes about 5–10 minutes.

1. R
The language we use for every analysis.

Windows: Download R for Windows
Mac: Download R for macOS (choose the Apple silicon build for M1–M4 Macs, Intel otherwise)



2. An IDE: Positron (recommended) or RStudio
The program you type R code into. Install one of them, after R.

Download Positron
Download RStudio Desktop



3. Posit Cloud account
A free browser-based RStudio. It is your backup if an installation fails on your laptop.

Sign up for Posit Cloud (the free plan is enough)



4. Google Antigravity 2.0
The AI coding assistant we use in the hands-on sessions.

Download Google Antigravity and sign in with your Google account



Check that it works
Open Positron or RStudio and type 1 + 1 in the Console. If you see [1] 2, you are ready.

title: Speakers
text:
Prof Dr Kamarul Imran Musa (KIM)
Professor of Epidemiology and Biostatistics at the School of Medical Sciences, Universiti Sains Malaysia. A medical epidemiologist and statistician, KIM teaches R, Quarto and reproducible data analysis for health research.





Assoc Prof Dr Kueh Yee Cheng (Erica)
Biostatistician at the School of Medical Sciences, Universiti Sains Malaysia. Erica teaches biostatistics and research methodology, with work in statistical modelling and forecasting for health research.
